Added and committed two regression tests covering the declaration load failures:

- A child declaration with an explicit ultimate payer loads without incorrectly requiring a selected parent payer.
- A company number stays paired with the `Company` donor kind when funder observations are grouped.

Both tests pass. Each also failed when I temporarily restored its original bug, confirming they catch the regressions. Formatting passed, and I updated [PR #26](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/26) with the test results.

The changes are committed on `fix/declaration-loader-parent-basis-20261008` as `c3640b0`. The local `todo.md` remains uncommitted. This follows the root-cause and behavior-focused testing principles: the tests exercise the loader’s observable results and demonstrate that each original failure is detected.

Raw source-control evidence.

- [PR #23](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/23), author `johnnylarner`, created 2026-10-08 08:07:03 UTC, merged 08:11:19 UTC. Its body explicitly states, “Link donors with the same usable normalized name … Other role combinations require stronger name, address, and score evidence.” Its tradeoff explicitly states, “Identity IDs are local to one ingestion run.” No comments, reviews, or review comments were returned. This is direct policy rationale, but does not identify this screenshot’s specific database rows.
- [PR #24](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/24), author `johnnylarner`, created 2026-10-08 08:10:17 UTC, merged 08:32:45 UTC. Its scope explicitly states, “funders retain exact source-name identities.” It also states, “Database schema and import behavior are unchanged.” No comments, reviews, or review comments were returned. This directly documents the earlier search/detail feature’s intentional identity scope.
- [PR #25](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/25), author `johnnylarner`, created 2026-10-08 09:00:29 UTC, merged 09:02:14 UTC. It adds resolved identities and funder aliases to the database loader. It says, “The configured project database was not migrated.” No comments/reviews/review comments were returned. It documents the transition to resolved imports, without promising migration or deletion of legacy source-name funders.
- Commit [`4877e594752b120bb8669a42654a974444ec64ac`](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/commit/4877e594752b120bb8669a42654a974444ec64ac), `johnnylarner`, 2026-10-08 09:33:40 +0200, “feat(resolution): link donors by exact normalized name,” introduced the exact donor-name acceptance policy. The classification requires exact `name_normalized` equality. The statistical rule also requires exact names, matching numbered-street addresses, and threshold. This is mechanics, not separate evidence of motivation.
- [Design document line 45](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-declaration-loader-fix-20261008/docs/funder-resolution-design.md:45) explicitly states, “fuzzy and alias matches receive no new acceptance rule.” [Line 49](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-declaration-loader-fix-20261008/docs/funder-resolution-design.md:49) states, “Fuzzy names and competing anchors remain review decisions.” These statements are direct policy rationale.
- [Design document line 23](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-declaration-loader-fix-20261008/docs/funder-resolution-design.md:23) says equal accepted company numbers seed one identity. [Line 33](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-declaration-loader-fix-20261008/docs/funder-resolution-design.md:33) says every statistical candidate needs at least one unanchored observation. Thus two separately anchored company IDs never merge through similarity alone.
- Most relevant existing test. [`shows_no_hsbc_duplicates`](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-declaration-loader-fix-20261008/exposed/tests/integration.rs:30) counts results by exact name strings. [Its assertions](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-declaration-loader-fix-20261008/exposed/tests/integration.rs:45) explicitly require each screenshot variant once: `HSBC UK Bank plc`, `HSBC UK Bank PLC`, and `HSBC UK (Ian Stuart, CEO)`. This test does not require one HSBC identity.
- Commit [`81ee9fc1d857883526334e28b081028190bce4e5`](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/commit/81ee9fc1d857883526334e28b081028190bce4e5), `johnnylarner`, 2026-09-24 10:34:14 +0100, originally named that test `shows_hsbc_duplicates` and expected five exact `plc` results, one `PLC`, and one CEO variant. [PR #6](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/6) has empty body and no discussions.
- Commit [`4d7110656863a25a20cff0a4e4c34af2a34c6619`](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/commit/4d7110656863a25a20cff0a4e4c34af2a34c6619), `johnnylarner`, 2026-09-25 13:12:38 +0100, renamed the test `shows_no_hsbc_duplicates` and changed only the exact `plc` count from five to one. The assertions preserving all three variants remained. [PR #8](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/8) has empty body and no discussions. This history directly proves earlier “deduplication” meant exact source-name rows, not entity resolution.

Queries searched included full file history, pickaxe for the HSBC test rename and counts, `rg -i hsbc` across `exposed`, `db`, and `docs`, identity-policy code and tests, PR bodies/reviews/comments for #23/#24/#25/#6/#8, and separate pull-request review comment endpoints. Only the old integration test contains “HSBC” in those source/document areas. No explicit HSBC-specific alias policy or resolution regression fixture was found. Live database/artifact evidence is still needed to distinguish legacy rows, conflicting company anchors, roles, and ingestion namespaces for the screenshot itself.
